claims.text: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease is the most common cause of elevated liver enzymes.
Within the non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) spectrum, only non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) progresses to cirrhosis.
Within the non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) spectrum, only non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) progresses to hepatocellular carcinoma.
The prevalence of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease is highest in populations with pre-existing metabolic conditions such as obesity and type II diabetes.
Diagnosis of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease relies on assessment tools including liver biopsy, radiological tests, and blood testing.

methodologies.name: Systematic PubMed Literature Search
methodologies.description: Systematic review searching PubMed (1980-2010) using terms related to NAFLD, NASH, fatty liver, steatosis, incidence, prevalence, and natural history.

limitations.text: Diagnosis of NAFLD across existing literature is heterogeneous and relies on a variety of distinct assessment tools.
Pediatric cohorts were excluded from the scope of this review.
